paper_title: MICROSCOPE mission: first constraints on the violation of the weak equivalence principle by a light scalar dilaton
notes: Curve traced from Fig. 5 (fig_de.png in the arXiv e-print), the solid black MICROSCOPE line: |d_e| for a dilaton coupled only to the electromagnetic sector, vs scalar mass m_phi [eV]. Boundary of the excluded (yellow) region for MICROSCOPE. The limit is flat at |d_e| ~ 2.3e-4 for m_phi from ~1e-24 up to ~1e-13 eV, then rises steeply, reaching |d_e|~1 near m_phi ~ 2e-11 eV; MICROSCOPE is insensitive to heavier masses. Text states it excludes |d_e|>1e-4 for 1e-18<m_phi/eV<1e-11 (2-sigma). Pixel calibration: x-axis 1e-24..1e-10 eV, y-axis 1e-9..1e0. This is the dilaton-to-photon (Damour-Donoghue d_e) result. The paper's other results (Figs 1/2: Yukawa |alpha| vs lambda for q=B and q=B-L scalar fifth force; Figs 3/4: massless/massive dilaton (D_mtilde, D_e) plane) are alternative parametrizations of the same MICROSCOPE eta=(-1+/-27)e-15 measurement; Fig 5 (d_e vs mass) is the plane matching the ScalarPhoton canonical variable. 2-sigma = 95% CL. Limit does not depend on a dark-matter density assumption (fifth-force/WEP test, not a DM search).
